about: About these leads

Leaflegal sends debt recovery enquiries from businesses that are owed money by other businesses and want a law firm to help recover it. Every enquiry is business to business. We do not send consumer debts, and we do not send enquiries from people or businesses who owe money and want help with their own debts.
Each enquiry goes to one firm only. It is never shared with a panel of firms or debt collection agencies and it is never resold after it has been delivered to you.

Business owners usually look for legal help with a debt after their own credit control has run out of road. Invoices have gone unpaid past their terms, reminders have been ignored or a customer has gone quiet. Some have a single large invoice that matters to their cash flow. Others have several smaller debts that have built up over months. Either way, they want a firm that acts quickly and tells them clearly what it will cost.

Our campaigns run on search, social media and helpful content aimed at business owners, finance managers and bookkeepers dealing with late payment. Each person answers a short set of questions about the debt, confirms that the debtor is a business and that they want paid help from a law firm, and gives their contact details. When an enquiry matches your criteria, we check it and send it to you straight away.

about.h3: Why business debt work suits bought leads

about: Commercial debt recovery is often repeat work. A business that has a good experience with one unpaid invoice will usually come back when the next one goes overdue, and may pass its whole collections book to the firm it trusts. An exclusive introduction gives you the chance to build that relationship from the first call, without a competing firm calling at the same time.

Leaflegal is not a law firm, a debt collection agency or a credit reference service. We do not give legal advice, we do not assess the strength of a claim and we do not contact debtors. We introduce a business creditor to one firm, and the advice and recovery work come from you.
Who enquires

Debt recovery enquiries come from businesses of all sizes, but most are small and medium sized firms without an in house legal team. You choose the kinds of matter you want, so a firm that prefers larger commercial claims does not have to take very small invoices.

list: Trades and construction businesses chasing payment for completed work
Wholesalers, manufacturers and distributors owed for goods supplied
Agencies, consultants and professional services firms with unpaid fees
Logistics, haulage and transport businesses
Recruitment businesses owed placement or temporary worker fees
Landlords of commercial premises owed rent by business tenants
Technology and software businesses with unpaid subscriptions or project fees
Letters before action
County Court and High Court claims
Statutory demands
Winding up and bankruptcy petitions against business debtors
Enforcement of judgments

about.h3: Where they are in the process

about: Some clients enquire as soon as an invoice is a few weeks overdue and want a solicitor's letter to prompt payment. Others have chased for months, tried a collection agency and now want to issue a claim. A smaller group already hold a judgment that has not been paid and want help with enforcement. Each lead tells you the age of the debt and gives a description in the client's own words, so you can see which stage you are dealing with.

Business creditors want three things. They want to know whether it is worth pursuing, what it will cost and how quickly something will happen. Many have been put off by open ended hourly rates, so a fixed fee for a letter before action or a clear scale for issuing a claim tends to land well. They also want to know whether they can recover interest and costs from the debtor, which you can explain on the first call.

Some clients have already used a collection agency or tried the online money claim service themselves. Knowing what has been tried before helps you explain what a law firm can add, and the description in the client's own words often covers this.
Lead details
Every debt recovery lead is the full record of what the client told us. The questions are short, but they give you the commercial basics you need to triage the enquiry before you pick up the phone.

about.h3: What each debt recovery lead includes

list: The client's name, business name, a verified UK mobile number and a verified email address
The rough amount owed
How old the debt is

about: Whether a debt is disputed changes the route a matter is likely to take. An undisputed debt may suit a letter before action followed quickly by a claim, while a disputed one may need a closer look at the contract, the correspondence and the evidence. Knowing the answer before you call helps you decide who in your team should speak to the client and how to frame the first conversation.

The age of the debt helps you judge urgency and spot limitation issues early. In England and Wales, most claims for a contract debt must be brought within six years of the date the money became due, although a written acknowledgment or a part payment can restart the clock. Older debts may also be harder to collect in practice, which is worth exploring with the client.

Every client confirms that the debtor is a business and that they want paid help, and their mobile number and email address are checked. Each one ticks one box to confirm they understand Leaflegal is an introduction service and a separate box to agree to one firm contacting them. We record the wording and the time and send it with the lead. Leads arrive as soon as they are checked, by email, to a shared inbox or straight into your CRM or case management system.
Working the lead
Debt recovery enquiries are commercial and practical. Business owners respond well to a firm that is quick, organised and clear about money.

A business owner who has decided to involve a solicitor usually wants to see something happen that week. Calling soon after a lead arrives shows the kind of service they can expect. Set up alerts so a fee earner or credit control lawyer sees each new lead quickly.

The lead gives you the amount, the age of the debt and whether it is disputed. On the first call you can ask for the invoice, the terms and any correspondence, and check basic points such as who the debtor is and whether it is still trading. A short, structured conversation reassures the client that their matter is in capable hands.

about.h3: Be clear about fees and recovery

about: Explain your fees for each stage, such as a letter before action, issuing a claim and enforcement, and what the client might be able to recover from the debtor. Many business creditors are not aware of statutory interest and compensation for late payment under the Late Payment of Commercial Debts (Interest) Act 1998, or of the fixed costs that may apply on court claims. A clear explanation of how this works in general often helps them decide.

After the call, a short email confirming the next step, the fee for that step and the documents you need keeps momentum. Business owners are busy, and a clear written summary makes it easy for them to say yes.

A client with one overdue invoice may have others. Asking about their wider credit control, their terms of business and how they chase late payers can open the door to ongoing work, such as reviewing their terms and conditions or handling collections on a regular basis.
The client agreed to be contacted after making an enquiry through Leaflegal. Mention that when you call, and cover any referral arrangement in your client care letter as your regulator requires.
Let us know which leads instruct and which do not. If disputed debts or very small invoices rarely convert for you, we can change your matching to send you more of the work that fits.
Compliance
Business debt recovery sits outside some of the heavier consumer rules, but your professional duties still apply in full. Leaflegal is set up to support them.

Every debt recovery enquiry is confirmed as business to business. We do not send consumer debts, which can bring separate regulatory requirements, and we do not send enquiries from people seeking debt advice. If a lead turns out to involve a consumer debtor, tell us and we will deal with it as your partner agreement sets out.

about.h3: Sole traders and the pre-action protocol

about: Some business debtors are sole traders or partnerships rather than companies. Where the debtor is an individual, including a sole trader, the Pre-Action Protocol for Debt Claims will usually apply, with its own requirements on the letter of claim and the time allowed for a response. The lead may not tell you the debtor's legal form, so it is worth checking on the first call.

Leaflegal is an introducer. Under the SRA Code of Conduct, you must make sure clients are told in writing about any financial arrangement with an introducer, and that it does not affect your independence or advice. Our consent wording tells every client we are paid by the firms we introduce them to, and we send it with every lead.

Debt recovery leads go to SRA regulated firms and CILEx regulated practices authorised for the work, including the conduct of litigation where needed. You are responsible for your own conflict checks, which matter if you already act for the debtor. Leaflegal, a trading name of Vertical Brands Ltd, is the controller for data collected on our forms. Once a lead is delivered, you are controller of your copy.
Read more about referral rules and introducers.
Pricing

You pay for each debt recovery lead we deliver, at a price agreed with you before you start. There is no retainer for advertising and no shared or recycled data, so you can measure each lead against the instructions and fees it produces.

Price depends on the matter types and the size of debts you choose to receive, and on how widely you want enquiries matched. Enquiries about larger debts, or about enforcement and insolvency routes, are usually priced differently from small invoice letters before action. We talk this through on a call and put a proposal together.

The minimum is 10 leads a month. Above that, you tell us how many your team can handle and we match to that number. You can set a monthly cap, change it and pause at any time, for example during a busy period of hearings or when a key fee earner is away.

Before your first lead, we agree a written partner agreement covering pricing, billing, volumes, delivery and the rules on invalid leads. If a lead has wrong contact details, turns out to be a consumer debt or falls outside your agreed criteria, tell us within the review period in your agreement and we will deal with it as the agreement says.

Onboarding starts with a 30 minute call with our team. We talk about the debt recovery work you want, the size of debts that suit you and your volume, and we show you a sample lead before you commit. You can apply to become a partner firm to book the call.
faqs: The leads
What is a debt recovery lead from Leaflegal?

It is an enquiry from a business that is owed money by another business and wants a law firm to help recover it. The client has told us roughly how much is owed, how old the debt is, whether it is disputed and how many debts are involved, confirmed their contact details and agreed to be contacted by one firm. We send it to you alone as soon as it is checked.
Do you send consumer debts?

No. Every debt recovery enquiry is business to business, and the client confirms the debtor is a business before the enquiry is submitted. We do not send debts owed by consumers, which can carry separate regulatory requirements, and we do not send enquiries from people who owe money and want debt advice. If a lead turns out to involve a consumer, tell us and we deal with it as your agreement says.
Are the leads exclusive?

Yes. Each enquiry is matched to one firm only and is never resold. We do not pass the same business to several firms or to collection agencies at the same time. You are the only firm that receives the client's details from us, which gives you room to make a proper first call and start building what may become a long term relationship.
Will I know whether the debt is disputed?

Yes. Each lead says whether the client believes the debtor disputes the debt. That helps you decide who should take the call and what route the matter might take. The answer comes from the client, so it is worth exploring on the first call, as some debtors raise disputes late or only after a solicitor's letter arrives.
What sizes of debt do you send?

Each lead includes the rough amount owed, and you can tell us the range of debts that suits your firm. Some firms are happy to take small invoices on a fixed fee basis, while others prefer larger commercial claims. We set your matching to the amounts you want and can change it later if your preferences change.
Can a lead involve more than one debt?

Yes. Each lead says how many debts the client wants help with. Some businesses come with a single overdue invoice, while others have several debtors or a backlog of late payers. Enquiries with several debts can be a good opening for ongoing collections work, and the description in the client's own words usually explains the background.
Do you send enquiries about statutory demands and winding up?

Yes, if you want them. You can choose to receive enquiries about statutory demands, winding up petitions and bankruptcy petitions against business debtors, as well as letters before action, court claims and enforcement. Each matter type can be switched on or off, so you only receive the kinds of debt recovery work your team handles.
Will I know if the debtor is still trading?

Not always. The lead tells you what the client knows, and the description in their own words may mention that the debtor has gone quiet, changed its name or stopped trading. Checking the debtor's status, for example at Companies House, is a sensible early step for your team. It helps you and the client decide whether recovery is realistic before costs are run up.
Volume and areas
How many leads will I receive?

That depends on the matter types, debt sizes and locations you choose and the enquiries our campaigns are generating at the time. The minimum is 10 leads a month. Above that, you set the number your team can handle and we match to it. We will give you an honest view on your call, but we cannot promise a fixed number.
Do clients need to be local to my office?

Not necessarily. Much commercial debt recovery work is done by phone, email and online court processes, so many firms are happy to act for businesses anywhere in England and Wales. If you prefer clients near your offices, we can limit matching to particular areas. Wider coverage usually means more matches.
Can I set a monthly cap?

Yes. You set the number of leads you want each month, as long as it is at least the minimum of 10. When you reach your cap, we stop matching enquiries to you until the next month. You can change your cap whenever your capacity changes, so your team is never sent more enquiries than it can deal with promptly.
Can I pause leads?

Yes. If your team is busy with hearings, a fee earner is away or you are changing systems, tell us and we will pause matching until you are ready again. Pausing does not end your partner agreement. When you want to restart, let us know and matching begins again as new enquiries come in.
Can leads go straight to our credit control team?

Yes. Leads can go by email to particular people, to a shared intake inbox, or straight into your CRM or case management system using a lead email address or a webhook. Many firms route debt recovery leads to a dedicated team so that new business creditors hear from a specialist straight away.
Do you send debts owed by businesses abroad?

Our debt recovery enquiries come from businesses in England and Wales. The description in the client's own words will usually mention it if the debtor is based overseas. If cross border recovery is not work you take on, tell us and we will set your matching to avoid it where we can, and you can raise any lead that does not fit.
Compliance
Do I need to disclose the referral fee?

Yes. Under the SRA Code of Conduct, you must make sure clients are told in writing about any financial arrangement with an introducer, and that it does not affect your independence or advice. Our consent wording tells every client that we are paid by the firms we introduce them to, and we send that wording with every lead so your client care letter can match it.
Does Leaflegal give advice or contact debtors?

No. Leaflegal is an introduction service. We do not give legal advice, assess the merits of a claim, contact debtors or collect money. We introduce a business creditor to one firm and the advice and recovery work are yours. We make clear to every client that we are not a law firm before they submit their enquiry.
Who can receive debt recovery leads?

SRA regulated firms and CILEx regulated practices authorised for the work, including the conduct of litigation where a matter goes to court. You are responsible for your own regulatory obligations, conflict checks and client identification. We ask about your regulation and the work you handle when you apply. You must tell us if your authorisation changes, so we can update or pause your matching.
What if the debtor is a sole trader?

Some business debtors are sole traders or partnerships. Where the debtor is an individual, including a sole trader, the Pre-Action Protocol for Debt Claims will usually apply, with its own requirements on the letter of claim and the response period. The lead may not say what legal form the debtor takes, so it is worth checking with the client early.
How is consent recorded?

Each client ticks one box confirming they have read our terms and privacy policy and understand that Leaflegal is an introduction service, and a second box agreeing to their details being shared with one firm that may contact them by phone, email or text. We record the exact wording and the time, and the record arrives with the lead.
Who controls the client's data?

Leaflegal, a trading name of Vertical Brands Ltd, is the controller for information collected through our forms. Once a lead is delivered, your firm becomes controller of its copy and handles it under your own privacy notice and UK data protection law. The consent covers contact about the client's enquiry. Marketing to them later needs their separate consent.
Pricing and terms
How much does a debt recovery lead cost?

There is no published price list. You pay per lead at a price agreed with you before you start, based on the matter types, debt sizes and locations you choose and the volume you want. We put a proposal together after your onboarding call, so you know the cost of every lead before the first one is delivered.
Is there a written agreement?

Yes. Your partner agreement covers pricing, billing, volumes, delivery and the rules on invalid leads, and it is in place before your first lead. Both sides know from the start what is charged, how leads are counted and how any problem with a lead is handled. We are happy to go through any part of it with you before you sign.
What counts as an invalid lead?

Your partner agreement sets this out. It usually covers wrong contact details, a consumer debt or an enquiry outside your agreed criteria. If you think a lead is invalid, tell us within the review period in your agreement and we will deal with it as the agreement says. A client deciding not to instruct does not by itself make a lead invalid.
Can I offer clients a fixed fee or a percentage?

How you charge clients is entirely for your firm, within your regulatory obligations. Many business creditors like a fixed fee for each stage, such as a letter before action, because it makes the cost of acting predictable. Whatever you offer, being clear about it on the first call tends to help clients decide.
What if the client pays the debt before we act?

Sometimes a debtor pays as soon as they hear a solicitor may be involved, or the client resolves things themselves. A lead is an introduction rather than a guaranteed instruction, so that does not make it invalid. Many firms find that a client whose debt was paid quickly comes back the next time an invoice goes unpaid, especially if the first call was helpful.
Getting started
How do I become a partner firm?

Apply to become a partner firm and book a 30 minute call with our team. We go through the debt recovery work you handle, the debt sizes that suit you, your locations and your volume. Then we agree your criteria and price, show you a sample lead and put your partner agreement in place before any leads are sent.
Can I see a sample lead first?

Yes. On your call we show you a sample debt recovery lead with every field, the format it arrives in and the consent record. You can see exactly how the amount, age, dispute status and number of debts are presented before you decide whether to go ahead. If you use a CRM, we can also talk through how the fields would map into it.
Is there a platform or login?

No. There is no portal to learn. Leads arrive by email, to a shared intake inbox, or straight into your CRM or case management system using a lead email address or a webhook. Your team works them in the systems they already use, which keeps things simple for a busy credit control or litigation team.
What should we prepare before the first lead?

Decide who calls new leads and how quickly. Prepare a short fee summary for each stage of a typical recovery, a standard list of documents to request after the call and a client care letter that covers the referral arrangement. Firms that have this ready usually find it easier to turn enquiries into instructions.
Can we change our criteria later?

Yes. Your matching is not fixed. If you find that disputed debts rarely suit you, or that you want more enforcement and insolvency work, tell us and we update your criteria. Feedback on which leads instruct and which do not helps us send you more of the debt recovery work that fits your team and your fee structure.
